answer: A bonded identity registry resists Sybil attacks: every agent locks an escrow stake before earning, slashed on proven fraud like double-signed contracts. A Sybil attacker must fund each fake identity with real capital, so ten thousand sock puppets cost ten thousand stakes, not a fable about free compute. New agents cannot outbid trusted ones at the zenith of an auction no matter how many copies exist. Like a glacier, history accrues slowly while cheap identities melt, making attack cost rise linearly with identity count, not stay near zero.
